clues.title: Plate: long white, one blue strip
text: Austria has long, **white** licence plates with the standard **blue EU strip** on the left.
NOTE: Italian plates have two blue strips, on both sides of the plate. Italian plates also tend to be noticeably shorter.
Swiss plates are long and white, but lack the blue strip.
clues.summary: Long white plates with the blue EU strip on the left only. Italian plates have two blue strips and are shorter; Swiss plates are long and white but have no blue strip.

differs.how: Italian plates are shorter with a blue strip on both sides
Swiss plates have no blue strip

clues.title: Bollard: white, black top, dark red reflector
text: Austria uses white** **bollards, with a **black top**. The colour of the reflector is **(dark) red or dark grey**.
Many bollards also feature a small nipple-shaped black cap on the top. Bollards sometimes have a [snow pole on top](https://goo.gl/maps/kkcrsQwXxFkn52rq8).
NOTE: Slovenia and Montenegro use the same bollards, but with bright red reflectors instead of grey or dark red. Germany uses simple white bollards with grey reflectors.

images.caption: White bollard with black top and dark red reflector; the arrow points to the black top

clues.summary: White post with a black top and a dark red or dark grey reflector. Many have a small black nipple-shaped cap, and some have a snow pole on top. Slovenia and Montenegro use similar ones with a bright red reflector.

differs.how: German posts are plain white with grey reflectors

clues.title: Chevron: white on red or red on yellow
text: Austria uses two colour schemes for **chevrons**:
- white on red
- red on yellow
NOTE: Germany mostly uses red on white chevrons, and rarely red on yellow.
clues.summary: Two colour styles: white on red, or red on yellow. Germany mostly uses red on white and only rarely red on yellow.

differs.how: Germany mostly uses red on white

clues.title: Pole: round wooden
text: Round **wooden** poles are the most common type of pole found in Austria.
clues.summary: Round wooden poles are the most common utility poles.

clues.title: Landscape: forested mountains, flatter east
text: Most of Austria is **mountainous** and covered in forests. However, some areas in the east and northeast are much more flat and agricultural.
clues.summary: Most of the country is mountainous and forested, but parts of the east and northeast are flatter and agricultural.

clues.title: Houses: light walls, wooden balconies, wide roofs
text: Alpine architecture is common in Austria and other countries in the Alps. Houses commonly have distinct **light **coloured walls, with **wooden **elements such as balconies or panelling around the top floor, with dark-coloured wooden roofs that extend outward. The roofs can sometimes be angled downward at the front and back. In addition, houses are also often multi-storeyed.
NOTE: Germany uses similar architecture in its southern states.
clues.summary: Alpine houses with light walls, wooden balconies or panelling on the top floor, and dark wooden roofs that stick out. Often several floors. Southern Germany builds in a similar way.

clues.title: Language: German letters Ä Ö Ü ß
text: The official language of Austria is **German**. The German language uses the special letters Ä, Ö, Ü and ß.

NOTE: The other majority German-speaking countries with coverage are Switzerland and Germany. In addition, German is spoken in [East Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German-speaking_Community_of_Belgium) and the Italian province of [South Tyrol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Tyrol).

images.caption: German text with the letters Ä Ö Ü ß shown large

clues.summary: German uses the special letters Ä, Ö, Ü and ß. Germany and Switzerland are also German-speaking, as are East Belgium and South Tyrol in Italy.

clues.title: Coverage: Gen 3 and Gen 4 only, never low-cam
text: You can tell the three German-speaking countries apart by **camera meta **alone:

- Austria only has **Generation 3** and Generation 4 coverage (the only exceptions being Generation 2 on [one road](https://goo.gl/maps/LebHyLrqsjkqyoZMA) in Burgenland, and several [ski resort trekkers](https://goo.gl/maps/pdquUsUJoNwZghxRA)).
- Germany only has Generation 4 coverage. (the only exceptions being spills and trekkers)
- Switzerland car coverage is always [low-cam](https://goo.gl/maps/Ey7aUdEn6vc76BZc8). This can be recognized by the much bigger car blur.

images.caption: Gen 3 (left) and Gen 4 (right) views of the same mountain road

clues.summary: Austria has mainly the older Gen 3 and the newer Gen 4. Germany has only Gen 4, and Switzerland is always low-cam with a much bigger car blur.

differs.how: Switzerland always has the big car blur of a low camera

clues.title: Google car: low camera, big round blur
text: Austria also has generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.
NOTE: Most of Western Europe also has smallcam.

images.caption: Four views of the same road: panned down, back, front and a good front blur

clues.summary: A low-mounted Gen 4 camera with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through, which makes it easy to miss. Most of Western Europe has it too.

clues.title: Direction sign: white, blue outline, special font
text: Direction signs have a white background, a **blue outline**, and a unique font.
clues.summary: Direction signs are white with a blue outline and a distinctive font.

clues.title: Sign: white town sign, blue outline
text: Similar white signs with a** **blue outline and unique font can also be seen at the **entrance of towns**.
NOTE: Germany uses [yellow town entrance signs](https://maps.app.goo.gl/fLnrUWoSDqzsyGxx5) with a black outline.
clues.summary: Similar white signs with a blue outline and the same font mark the entrance of towns. Germany uses yellow town signs with a black outline.

differs.how: German town signs are yellow with a black outline

clues.title: Sign: green local-facility signs
text: **Green** signs can commonly be seen, giving directions to different local facilities.
clues.summary: Green signs are common, pointing to local facilities.

clues.title: Pedestrian sign: two dashed lines, no stripes
text: **Pedestrian signs** have a unique design: instead of zebra stripes, they have two horizontal dashed lines.
NOTE: All neighbouring countries have pedestrian signs with zebra stripes.
clues.summary: Pedestrian signs show two horizontal dashed lines instead of zebra stripes. All neighbouring countries use zebra stripes.

clues.title: Sign: mounted with four metal clips
text: Road signs in Austria are sometimes mounted by **four metal clips**, which is unique within central Europe. However, plenty of Austrian signs are attached in other ways.

images.caption: A round sign mounted with four metal clips; red arrows point to the clips

clues.summary: Road signs are sometimes held by four metal clips, which is unique in central Europe. Many are fixed other ways, though.

clues.title: Route marker: blue with white number and comma
text: **Road markers** are blue with white numbers. They have one decimal separated by a comma, making them very recognizable.
NOTE: Slovenian road markers are white. And German markers have a thin white outline.
clues.summary: Blue markers with white numbers that have one decimal after a comma. Slovenian markers are white, and German ones have a thin white outline.

differs.how: German markers have a thin white outline

clues.title: Sign: bus stop with yellow-green circle and H
text: Austrian **bus stop signs** contain a yellow and green circle with the letter **H**.
NOTE: This design is relatively unique in Europe. The only other country with similar bus stop signs is Germany.
clues.summary: Bus stop signs show a yellow and green circle with the letter H. Germany is the only other country with similar signs.

clues.title: Sign: one-way sign says EINBAHN
text: These one-way traffic signs, with the word **‘EINBAHN’** written on them, are unique to Austria.
NOTE: In Germany there will be “Einbahnstraße” written on the sign.
clues.summary: One-way signs with the word EINBAHN are unique. German ones say Einbahnstraße.

clues.title: Sign: No Stopping with Anfang or Ende
text: “No Stopping” and “No Waiting” signs in Austria will often have the words “Anfang” or “Ende” (meaning “beginning” and “end”) written on, or below, them.
clues.summary: No Stopping and No Waiting signs often have Anfang (beginning) or Ende (end) written on or below them.

clues.title: Sign: dead end with white upside-down T
text: These simple dead-end signs with a **white upside down T** are mostly unique to Austria.
Most countries in Europe use [this sign](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cB2CMCs6fQTNTZPQ8).
NOTE: Older coverage in Switzerland can be seen using [this design](https://maps.app.goo.gl/yv3PkLHesS63WCYD7) as well.
clues.summary: Simple dead-end signs with a white upside-down T are mostly unique. Most of Europe uses a different design, and older Swiss coverage used this one too.

differs.how: Older Swiss coverage used the same sign

clues.title: Pole: yellow gas marker, like a snow pole
text: These **yellow **natural gas poles, which resemble snow poles, are unique to Austria.
clues.summary: Yellow natural gas poles that look like snow poles. Unique here.

clues.title: Landscape: height shows the region
text: **Elevation** is very important when region-guessing Austria based on landscape alone.

The central and western parts of Austria are the most mountainous. The flatter areas are found in the east, mostly near the borders. Note that “flat” is a relative concept in Austria: even in the flat areas, rolling hills are still common.
clues.summary: Height is key. The centre and west are the most mountainous; flatter parts are in the east near the borders, though even those have rolling hills.

clues.title: Route marker: A-road numbers rise westward
text: A map of Austrian **A-roads **can be seen here, following the general trend of increasing in number from east to west.
_You can click the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Motorway numbers get bigger the further west you go.

clues.title: Route marker: B-roads rise westward
text: Austrian **B-roads**, indicated by white text inside of a blue rectangle, also follow the general trend of increasing in number from east to west.
An important exception to this are roads 222-230, which are located inside the state of Vienna.
_You can click the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: B-roads, white text in a blue rectangle, also rise in number from east to west. The exception is 222 to 230, around the capital.

clues.title: Flags: each state has its own flag
text: Each Austrian state has its own **unique flag**, shown in the image.
_You can click the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Every state has its own flag, which you may see on buildings.

clues.title: Buses: each state has its own bus company
text: Each Austrian state has its own **unique **bus company, the logo of which can be seen on the side of buses.
_You can click the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Each state has its own bus company, with its logo on the side of buses.

clues.title: Bus stop: neon-yellow poles
text: Bus stops consisting of **neon-yellow poles** are found in Vorarlberg.
clues.summary: Bus stops made of neon-yellow poles are in Vorarlberg, the far west.

clues.title: Pole: yellow and white stripes
text: These **yellow and white stripes** around poles and signposts are found in Vorarlberg.

images.caption: Pole with yellow and white stripes; the red circle at top left magnifies the stripes

clues.summary: Yellow-and-white stripes around poles and signposts are found in Vorarlberg, the far west.

clues.title: Kilometre marker: white
text: **White kilometre markers** can be found in Vorarlberg as well as on a road in [western Salzburg](https://maps.app.goo.gl/sDKDbQ2Czn1zkd59A).
clues.summary: White kilometre markers are in Vorarlberg and on one road in western Salzburg.

clues.title: Road: large white painted square
text: A large **white** **painted square** in the middle of the road can be found next to kilometre markers in Salzburg.
clues.summary: A big white painted square in the middle of the road next to kilometre markers means Salzburg state.

clues.title: Sign: green Güterweg sign
text: **Green** “[Güterweg](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%BCterweg)” signs are found in Burgenland.

images.caption: A green Güterweg sign on a post in a field

clues.summary: Green Güterweg (local farm road) signs are found in Burgenland, in the east.

clues.title: Sign: white Güterweg, black outline
text: **White** “Güterweg” signs with a **black outline** are mainly found in Upper Austria.

images.caption: A white Güterweg sign with a black outline

clues.summary: White Güterweg signs with a black outline are mainly found in Upper Austria.

clues.title: Sign: yellow and blue borders
text: In Lower Austria, you may find signs with **yellow and blue sign borders**, corresponding to the [flag of the region](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Flag_of_Lower_Austria_%28state%29.svg/2560px-Flag_of_Lower_Austria_%28state%29.svg.png).

images.caption: A white sign on metal posts in tall grass with yellow and blue borders

clues.summary: In Lower Austria, signs may have yellow and blue borders matching the regional flag.

clues.title: Plants: vineyards in the far east
text: **Vineyards** are limited to the far eastern part of the country.
You can find a very precise map [here](https://vineyards.com/photos/maps/Austria%20Wine%20Map.png). Notably, there are a lot of vineyards close to Vienna and around Lake Neusiedl.
clues.summary: Vineyards are limited to the far east, with many near Vienna and around Lake Neusiedl.

clues.title: Landscape: tallest sharp Alps
text: The **highest parts of the Alps** are found in the west and central parts of the country.

The tallest mountains are found in the panhandle of Austria, on the Italian border. These mountains can be recognized by their generally sharper peak and [grander appearance](https://www.google.com/maps/@47.1389055,10.2855153,3a,75y,66.33h,92.53t/data=!3m7!1e1!3m5!1sTDJ_tFCAlBIH4nUIgmkiMw!2e0!5s20200901T000000!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu).
clues.summary: The highest Alps are in the west and centre. The tallest mountains are in the narrow southern strip on the Italian border, with sharper peaks and a grander look.

clues.title: Google car: tin foil antenna
text: This unique **tin foil antenna** can be found in western** **Austria, mostly near the Swiss border.
NOTE: This antenna is unique to Austria.

images.caption: Tin foil antenna on the car's roof, marked with a red circle

clues.summary: A tin-foil-looking antenna, mostly in western Austria near the Swiss border. Unique here.

clues.title: Street sign: dark blue, white serif, district no.
text: **Vienna street signs** are extremely recognizable dark blue plaques with a traditional-looking white serif font. The number at the start will indicate which district you are in (see the map).
_You can click the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: The capital's street signs are dark blue plaques with a traditional white serif font. The number at the start is the district.

clues.title: Street sign: each big city has its own
text: Most other major cities in Austria also have their own **unique street signs**.
NOTE: Many of the arbitrary blue ones can look similar, but the 4 listed in the graphic can be differentiated by:
- Vienna - District Number
- Salzburg - Unique Font
- Klagenfurt - Irregular White Border
- St Polten - Rounded White Border
_You can click the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Many cities have their own street signs. The blue ones look alike, but can be told apart: Vienna by district number, Salzburg by its font, Klagenfurt by an irregular white border, St Pölten by a rounded white border.

clues.title: Pole: red-and-white tape like the flag
text: Poles in Vienna and [Innsbruck](https://goo.gl/maps/MWpqa8t1cVzunLrz9) feature these **red**-and-**white **pieces of tape that look like the Austrian flag. They can be differentiated by the fact that the tapes in [Vienna](https://goo.gl/maps/N4tkGXcAt1sbjxNy7) are thinner, and there are typically two on each pole.
clues.summary: Red-and-white tape resembling the national flag appears on poles in Vienna and Innsbruck. In Vienna the tape is thinner and there are usually two on each pole.

clues.title: Landscape: huge lake in the far west
text: **Lake Constance** (known in German as the Bodensee) is a large lake on the western border of Austria. It can be recognized by its vastness, which is not seen in other lakes within the mountainous part of the country.
clues.summary: Lake Constance (Bodensee) on the western border is recognisable by its vast size, unlike other lakes in the mountains.
